<STRUCT_0001>
We briefly discuss unramified morphisms before the (perhaps) more interesting
class of <ACCENT_0001>tale morphisms. Recall that a ring map <MATH_0001> is <TEXTITOPEN_0001>unramified<TEXTITCLOSE_0001>
if it is of finite type and <MATH_0002> (this is the definition
of <REF_0001>). A ring map <MATH_0003> is called <TEXTITOPEN_0002>G-unramified<TEXTITCLOSE_0002> if it
is of finite presentation and <MATH_0004> (this is the definition of
<REF_0002>). See
Algebra, Definition <REF_0003>.

Let <MATH_0001> be a morphism of schemes.
<STRUCT_0001>
<STRUCT_0002> We say that <MATH_0002> is <TEXTITOPEN_0001>unramified at <MATH_0003><TEXTITCLOSE_0001> if
there exists an affine open neighbourhood <MATH_0004>
of <MATH_0005> and affine open <MATH_0006>
with <MATH_0007> such that the induced ring map
<MATH_0008> is unramified.
<STRUCT_0003> We say that <MATH_0009> is <TEXTITOPEN_0002>G-unramified at <MATH_0010><TEXTITCLOSE_0002> if
there exists an affine open neighbourhood <MATH_0011>
of <MATH_0012> and affine open <MATH_0013>
with <MATH_0014> such that the induced ring map
<MATH_0015> is G-unramified.
<STRUCT_0004> We say that <MATH_0016> is <TEXTITOPEN_0003>unramified<TEXTITCLOSE_0003> if it is unramified
at every point of <MATH_0017>.
<STRUCT_0005> We say that <MATH_0018> is <TEXTITOPEN_0004>G-unramified<TEXTITCLOSE_0004> if it is G-unramified
at every point of <MATH_0019>.
<STRUCT_0006>

<STRUCT_0001>
Note that a G-unramified morphism is unramified. Hence any result for
unramified morphisms implies the corresponding result for G-unramified
morphisms. Moreover, if <MATH_0001> is locally Noetherian then there is no difference
between G-unramified and unramified morphisms, see
Lemma <REF_0001>.
A pleasing feature of this definition is that the set of points
where a morphism is unramified (resp.<SPACE_0001>G-unramified) is automatically open.
